Bathroom mirrors · Updated November 8, 2026

The right bathroom mirror is sized to the vanity, not the wall.

The glass itself rarely separates one mirror from another. What buyers regret is a mirror wider than the cabinet below it, an edge that corrodes in a steamy room, or an LED model bought before anyone checked for an outlet. We compare mirrors on those three points, using spec sheets, current Amazon prices and what verified owners report.

Our method

How we research

What we compare

  • Width: about 2 to 4 inches narrower than the vanity cabinet. Framed sizes include the frame, so the glass is smaller than the label.
  • Light and power: front-lit or backlit LEDs, a defogger pad, and whether it plugs into an outlet or has to be hardwired.
  • Edges and frame: sealed, beveled or metal-framed edges hold up to humidity better than raw-cut glass or wood frames.
  • Price: Amazon's current price, checked every night.
  • What verified owners report after months of daily use.

What we don't do

We don't run a lab, and we don't claim to have installed or handled these products ourselves. Our picks come from published specifications, current Amazon prices and what verified owners report again and again.

Every Amazon link on this site is an affiliate link. It never decides the ranking.

Before you buy

Common questions

What size mirror should go over my vanity?

Choose a mirror 2 to 4 inches narrower than the vanity cabinet, so a 36-inch vanity takes a mirror 32 to 34 inches wide. Leave a few inches between the backsplash and the bottom edge so splashes land on tile, not glass. Our mirror sizing guide covers double vanities and round mirrors.

Does an LED mirror need an electrician?

Not always. Many LED mirrors plug into a standard outlet, so the job is mostly hanging a heavy mirror on solid anchors. Hardwired models connect to the wall circuit and need an electrician, or someone comfortable working with the power off. Check for an outlet or junction box before you order; our LED vs regular mirror comparison covers the rest.

Why do the edges of a bathroom mirror turn black?

That is desilvering: moisture reaches the silver backing from the edges and corrodes it. Raw-cut frameless edges are the most exposed, while sealed, beveled or framed edges slow it down. Running the exhaust fan during and after showers, and spraying cleaner on the cloth instead of the glass, keeps water away from the backing.
